# Incident Report — 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** | Consistent source IP across all suspicious traffic |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | Observed in Ethernet/ARP frames where `ip.src == 172.17.0.99` |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DNS dynamic-update queries at start of capture (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT`, `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com`, `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.local`); confirmed again in Kerberos AS-REQ for service principal `host/desktop-rnvo9at.bepositive.com` |
| Logged-in Windows user | **afletcher** | `kerberos.CNameString == afletcher` in TGS-REQ/AS-REQ exchanges with the domain controller (realm `BEPOSITIVE.COM` / `BEPOSITIVE`) |
| Domain / DC | `bepositive.com`, DC `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com` at 172.17.0.17 (MAC `00:23:ae:50:ba:fd`) | LDAP/Kerberos SRV lookups and Kerberos SNames |

Note: the LAN uses RFC1918 172.17.0.0/24 addressing, which is why Suricata fired benign "ET POLICY Reserved Internal IP Traffic" alerts on normal DNS/SMB/Kerberos traffic between the workstation and its own domain controller — this is expected AD traffic, not malicious in itself.

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer) — **signature-confirmed**.

The Suricata/ET Pro alert `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` fired 48 times against POST requests from 172.17.0.99 to `79.124.78.197`. This was independently corroborated by direct inspection of the traffic:

- The victim performs an initial gate check-in (`GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U`) that returns a pipe-delimited bot record: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`.
- A follow-up `POST /index.php` exchanges an encrypted binary blob (105 bytes, e.g. `b563a25c...fcb062`) — consistent with an encrypted C2 config/task pull.
- The host then beacons repeatedly to `POST /foots.php` (96 requests observed over the ~59-minute capture, roughly every 60–90 seconds) using the fixed request format `<len>|<GUID>|<key>|<base64 blob>`, e.g.:
  ```
  101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
  ```
  Each beacon uses a static bot GUID (`30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`) with a rotating short key and an encrypted/base64 payload — the server always answers with `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and an empty body, typical of a stealer ack-beacon.
- All requests share a static spoofed User-Agent string (fake IE7/Windows NT 10.0/Trident) that does not match a real browser, matching the `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser` alert.

No malware binary (PE/EXE) was observed transferred over HTTP, SMB, or FTP in this capture, so no dropped-file SHA256 hash can be produced from the traffic — the initial compromise likely happened via encrypted channel (see §3) or prior to this capture window.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control endpoint
- **79.124.78.197:80/TCP** — primary Koi Stealer C2 (gate + beacon server, `Server: nginx`)

### Malicious/suspicious URLs
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (gate check-in, affiliate/subid `qIOuKk7U`)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (encrypted config POST)
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (recurring stealer beacon, 96 occurrences)

### Suspicious pre-infection contact (probable delivery vector)
- **46.254.34.201:443/TCP**, TLS SNI **`www.bellantonicioccolato.it`** — a ~102-second TLS session opened at capture time 153.3s, immediately preceding the first Koi Stealer gate/beacon traffic to 79.124.78.197 at 155.4s. Content is TLS-encrypted so it cannot be directly confirmed as the delivery mechanism, but the timing (this session closes right as the C2 checkins begin) and the unrelated/out-of-place nature of the domain (an Italian confectionery site with no other reason to be contacted by this host) make it the most likely infection vector. No DNS query resolving to either 46.254.34.201 or 79.124.78.197 appears anywhere in the capture, indicating both addresses/connections were hardcoded rather than looked up.

### Malicious domain
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (TLS SNI, associated with 46.254.34.201, likely compromised/abused legitimate site used in the delivery chain)

### Transferred file names / hashes
- None observed. No executable content, Content-Disposition header, or PE (`MZ`) payload was transferred in cleartext over HTTP/SMB/FTP anywhere in this capture. The only file-like exchanges are the encrypted beacon blobs above, which are not recoverable as named files or hashable binaries from this pcap alone.

### Legitimate/benign traffic ruled out
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` (`/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` → response body `****`) is normal Adobe ARM telemetry, not malicious.
- Traffic to `*.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `*.windowsupdate.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `sso.godaddy.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org`, etc. is standard OS/Office/telemetry/CRL traffic, unrelated to the infection.
- The SMB/NTLMSSP/Kerberos "GPL"/"ET" alerts at 172.17.0.99 ↔ 172.17.0.17 (SMBv1, NTLMSSP overflow, IPC$ access, TRANSACTION DOS) at 17:33 UTC align with normal domain-join/authentication chatter with the DC and are not associated with the Koi Stealer C2 activity, which starts about two minutes later.

## Summary

Windows workstation **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **BEPOSITIVE\afletcher**, made a suspicious encrypted TLS connection to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201:443), immediately followed by a gate check-in and recurring beacon traffic to **79.124.78.197:80**, signature-matched by Suricata/ET Pro as **Win32/Koi Stealer** C2 traffic. The infection persisted and beaconed roughly every 60–90 seconds for the remainder of the ~59-minute capture (96 total `/foots.php` POSTs), exfiltrating base64/encrypted data with a fixed bot GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`.
